title: VI-Rig: 4 IMUs + 3 cameras
intro: Our rig: a FLIR Blackfly and a RealSense T265 fisheye pair, all global shutter, with four IMUs from 100 to 500 Hz.

image.alt: The VI-Rig: a Blackfly camera, a RealSense T265 and four IMUs on one plate

solved.reason: not run: one IMU per run; no run holds the whole rig

families.read_first: Kalibr's intrinsics and baselines are inputs from its own camera-only calibration; its td and lever are solved given them. Data settings differ: see Notes.
notes: Basalt cannot calibrate T6 — one IMU per run (the rig has four) and frames grouped by exact stamp (the t265 pair and the Blackfly share none), so no single run holds the rig.

MVIS uses two corners per tag, non-base cameras at 4 Hz or lower and an estimated board shape; Kalibr has none of these. Every tool uses the same IMU noise, measured at rest (the rig's noisiest IMU, one set for all four IMUs). Kalibr's runs date from 2026-11-08.
Kalibr starts from its own camera-only calibration of each bag. Every tool uses the same IMU noise, measured at rest on the rig's noisiest IMU.

families.title: 3 GS cameras — camera calibration
families.read_first: MVIS runs the Blackfly and the t265 pair separately, so it has no baseline to the Blackfly; Kalibr solves the three cameras jointly.
notes: MVIS uses two corners per tag and estimates the board shape; Kalibr uses all four corners and assumes a flat board.

MVIS runs camera-only per bag, the Blackfly alone and the t265 pair (the rig's cameras share no frame stamps), so it has no baseline to the Blackfly; Kalibr's 10 camera-only runs solve the three cameras jointly.

t265 pair (kb4, fisheye 2 snapped onto fisheye 1) and Blackfly alone (pinhole-radtan8, a different model from radtan: its intrinsics are shown only); no camera-only Basalt run holds both devices, so no baselines to the Blackfly.
